headline: DOH Records 5,835 Leptospirosis Cases Nationwide as Flood Exposure Drives Recent Rise
seoTitle: DOH Records 5,835 Leptospirosis Cases Nationwide | FMB News
seoDescription: DOH data show 5,835 leptospirosis cases and 358 deaths nationwide, with recent flooding increasing concern over exposure.
deck: DOH data cited by multiple reports show 5,835 cases and 358 deaths this year, while the recent case trend has risen after widespread flooding.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Department of Health data cited by multiple Philippine reports show 5,835 leptospirosis cases nationwide this year and 358 deaths.

The largest reported case totals included 1,733 in Metro Manila, 632 in Central Luzon and 561 in Cagayan Valley. While the year-to-date total was reported lower than the comparable period in 2025, the recent two-week trend increased by about 29 percent.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Leptospirosis is a bacterial disease associated with exposure to water or soil contaminated by infected animal urine. Concern typically rises after severe flooding because residents, responders and commuters may have unavoidable contact with floodwater.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The current rise comes as many communities are still recovering from prolonged flooding, creating a second public-health burden on households and hospitals.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for updated DOH surveillance data, local case clusters and hospital-capacity advisories. FMB News is using 358 deaths after the earlier conflicting figure was cross-checked against multiple current reports citing DOH data.
